_comment: First 10 champions (GCD 9.x). Import via Tools > Project D > Import Champion Data. Ability names/mechanics are ORIGINAL Project D proposals; stats are placeholders for telemetry/playtest tuning. sourceReleaseDate = original Japanese release of the source title. lore/playstyle/strengths/weaknesses/tips feed the Champion Select screen and codex.

champions.title: The Crystal's Vanguard
champions.coreFantasy: Lawful guardian who leads from the front, converting protection into offense.
champions.lore: One of the four Warriors of Light chosen to bear the crystals in the world's oldest recorded conflict. In the Dissidia arena he is the steadfast champion of Cosmos, embodying order, duty, and unshakable resolve. He fights not for glory but to shield those behind him, and his blade shines brightest when an ally is in danger.
champions.playstyle: A frontline anchor who wants to be first into a fight and last to leave. Warrior of Light soaks pressure with Shield of Light, peels for carries with Vanguard Step, and turns every block into an empowered counter through his Crystal Resolve passive. Reward: consistency and protection over flashy burst.
champions.strengths: Excellent single-target peel; strong frontline durability; low mechanical barrier; great for teaching the Vanguard role.
champions.weaknesses: Limited hard crowd control; modest kill pressure; can be kited by long-range poke; relies on allies to convert his setup.
champions.tips: Hold Shield of Light toward the enemy's biggest damage source, not just the nearest unit. Use Vanguard Step onto an ally to reposition defensively, or onto an enemy to displace them off your carry. Pop Shining Bulwark BEFORE diving, so the mark-and-field is active as the fight opens.

passive.name: Crystal Resolve
passive.notes: Blocking or controlling an enemy builds Resolve; the next Shield of Light is empowered and heals briefly.

q.name: Radiant Cut
q.notes: Short sword arc; the outer edge deals bonus damage and applies a brief slow.

w.name: Shield of Light
w.notes: Directional guard that greatly reduces frontal damage for a short window, then releases a light wave.

e.name: Vanguard Step
e.notes: Dash to an ally or enemy; arriving on an enemy briefly displaces them.

ultimate.name: Shining Bulwark
ultimate.notes: Creates a protective field granting allies resistances and marks nearby enemies for focused defense.

champions.title: Knight of the Endless Cycle
champions.coreFantasy: Relentless armored knight built for extended disruption.
champions.lore: The fallen knight who declared he would knock the heroes all down, bound to a time loop that resurrects him across ages. In Dissidia he is a servant of Chaos, reveling in perpetual battle. Every wound only sharpens his resolve, and his massive blade carves through formations that dare to hold their ground.
champions.playstyle: A grinding bruiser who thrives in prolonged skirmishes. Garland stacks armor and power through Cycle of Strife the longer he keeps swinging, so he wants drawn-out fights rather than quick trades. He pulls enemies in, locks them down, and out-sustains them as his passive snowballs.
champions.strengths: Strong sustained damage and durability in long fights; multiple soft controls; excellent dive and disruption; punishes clustered enemies.
champions.weaknesses: Weak burst; passive resets out of combat, so hit-and-run enemies deny his ramp; mobility-reliant compositions can disengage from him.
champions.tips: Open with Chain of Ruin to slow, recast to lunge in, then Greatblade Reap to pull edge targets together. Iron Advance is unstoppable during wind-up — use it to force through crowd control. Save Chaosbringer for a 5-man fight; the repeated shockwaves reward staying in melee.

passive.name: Cycle of Strife
passive.notes: Ability hits grant stacking armor and power (capped); stacks fade after leaving combat.

q.name: Greatblade Reap
q.notes: Broad sweep that pulls edge targets slightly inward.

w.name: Iron Advance
w.notes: Unstoppable wind-up into a short charge that knocks back on impact.

e.name: Chain of Ruin
e.notes: Throws a chain blade that slows and enables a recast lunge to the target.

ultimate.name: Chaosbringer
ultimate.notes: Empowers size, reach, and releases repeated shockwaves for a limited time.

champions.title: Wielder of the Wild Rose
champions.coreFantasy: Versatile rebel who rotates among weapon ranges.
champions.lore: A young rebel of Fynn who took up arms against a tyrannical empire, famed for mastering every weapon he touches. The wild rose is his rebellion's symbol of hope. In Dissidia he fights with an entire arsenal at once, switching seamlessly between sword, spear, bow, and axe as the moment demands.
champions.playstyle: A flexible ranged carry who rewards weaving different weapon types. Firion's Arsenal Rhythm passive builds power whenever he alternates ability classes, so his best damage comes from a varied combo rather than spamming one button. He can poke from range with the bow, then step in for a Blood Blade heal.
champions.strengths: Adaptable range; strong mixed poke and sustain; self-healing in extended trades; flexible build paths (crit or bruiser).
champions.weaknesses: Lower peak DPS than a pure crit marksman; combo-dependent; squishy if forced into melee without cover; punished by hard engage.
champions.tips: Chain Spearline -> Bow Volley -> Blood Blade to keep Arsenal Rhythm stacked and heal off the finisher. Bow Volley reveals — use it to check brush before rotating. Aim Wild Rose Arsenal's final shot at a low-health target; the finishing projectile is where most of the ultimate's damage lands.

passive.name: Arsenal Rhythm
passive.notes: Using a different ability class than your last grants a stacking adaptive bonus.

q.name: Spearline
q.notes: Piercing thrust with a sweet spot at maximum reach.

w.name: Bow Volley
w.notes: Targeted area volley that reveals struck enemies.

e.name: Blood Blade
e.notes: Close strike that restores health based on damage dealt.

ultimate.name: Wild Rose Arsenal
ultimate.notes: Rapid sequence of weapon projections ending in a controllable finishing shot.

champions.title: Sovereign of Palamecia
champions.coreFantasy: Patient controller who turns terrain into a trap.
champions.lore: The ruthless ruler of Palamecia who conquered through cunning and dark sorcery, ambitious enough to seize both Heaven and Hell. In Dissidia he serves Chaos as a schemer who never dirties his own hands, seeding the battlefield with hidden traps and letting his enemies destroy themselves upon them.
champions.playstyle: A zone-control mage who plays chess, not checkers. The Emperor sets Hell Snare traps and Thunder Sigils ahead of a fight, marking enemies Exposed when they trigger separate traps. He is strongest defending a chokepoint or objective where his prepared ground funnels opponents into his mines.
champions.strengths: Dominant area denial; strong objective and chokepoint control; heavy burst on trapped targets; excellent disengage with Imperial Repulse.
champions.weaknesses: Weak when caught without setup; low mobility; telegraph-reliant; struggles in open-field skirmishes and against hard engage assassins.
champions.tips: Pre-place Hell Snare in brush or behind terrain where it's hardest to see. Trigger one trap, then a second to apply Exposed for a burst window. Imperial Repulse can push a diving assassin back onto your own Thunder Sigil. Pandemonium arms traps faster — drop it on an objective the enemy must contest.

passive.name: Dominion
passive.notes: Enemies hit by two separate traps become Exposed, taking bonus magic damage.

q.name: Thunder Sigil
q.notes: Delayed lightning seal on the ground.

w.name: Hell Snare
w.notes: Hidden zone that arms, then roots the first enemy to enter; visible only at close range.

e.name: Imperial Repulse
e.notes: Cone blast that pushes enemies back toward prepared zones.

ultimate.name: Pandemonium
ultimate.notes: Creates a domain where traps arm faster and periodic bolts strike Exposed targets.

champions.title: Prodigy of the Forbidden Jobs
champions.coreFantasy: Young adaptable hero who changes between nimble and arcane play.
champions.lore: A gifted youth chosen by the crystals, whose true strength blossoms only when others underestimate him. The Onion Knight can master any job the crystals reveal. In Dissidia he darts between the reckless speed of the Ninja and the calculated range of the Sage, a small figure with a startling ceiling.
champions.playstyle: A high-skill assassin-mage hybrid built around stance dancing. Job Shift toggles between Ninja (mobility, empowered Swift Blade) and Sage (range, empowered Dualcast), and the Job Mastery passive rewards alternating physical and magical casts. Mastering the swap unlocks burst combos others can't replicate.
champions.strengths: Very high skill ceiling and burst potential; flexible engage and poke; strong target access; can adapt to physical or magical threats mid-fight.
champions.weaknesses: Punishing skill floor; extremely squishy; heavily combo-dependent; a mistimed stance swap wastes the whole rotation.
champions.tips: In Ninja stance, Swift Blade resets on a marked target — chain kills through minions. Swap to Sage before Dualcast for the empowered double bolt, then swap back for the escape. Job Mastery wants you to alternate: physical -> magical -> physical. Mastered Jobs briefly gives you BOTH stances; use it to open AND escape.

passive.name: Job Mastery
passive.notes: Alternating between physical and magical casts empowers the next opposite-type ability.

q.name: Swift Blade
q.notes: Dash slash; cooldown partially resets on a killing blow or marked target.

e.name: Job Shift
e.notes: Toggle Ninja (mobility) or Sage (range), modifying Swift Blade and Dualcast.

ultimate.name: Mastered Jobs
ultimate.notes: Briefly activates both stances at once and grants a finishing recast.

champions.title: Herald of the Void
champions.coreFantasy: Otherworldly entity that controls lanes with void pressure.
champions.lore: The embodiment of the Void, an entity that exists to return all things to nothingness. Neither cruel nor kind, she simply is the end of all creation. In Dissidia she drifts above the battlefield, her particle-beam tentacles raking lanes with cold, impersonal annihilation.
champions.playstyle: A long-range control mage who suffocates a lane. Cloud of Darkness stacks Void on enemies with sustained beams to amplify her damage, then zones with Dark Flood and detonates everything with World of Nothing. She wants space and vision to fire her narrow Zero Ray safely.
champions.strengths: Exceptional range and lane zoning; strong scaling; area detonation in teamfights; brief untargetability for safety.
champions.weaknesses: Immobile and easily collapsed on; narrow skillshots demand accuracy; low early burst; Void ramp needs uninterrupted uptime.
champions.tips: Land Zero Ray at max range to stack Void without stepping up. Dark Flood zones a chokepoint and slows dive attempts. Save Unbound Form to dodge the key enemy engage — it's untargetable but you can't cast during it. Open teamfights with World of Nothing on the cluster to reduce their vision and pop stored Void.

passive.name: Particle Beam
passive.notes: Sustained attacks apply Void stacks, increasing damage dealt to that target.

q.name: Zero Ray
q.notes: Narrow beam; range extends after a brief charge.

w.name: Dark Flood
w.notes: Advancing field that slows enemies inside it.

e.name: Unbound Form
e.notes: Brief untargetable drift; cannot cast other abilities during it.

ultimate.name: World of Nothing
ultimate.notes: Expanding void zone that reduces enemy vision and detonates accumulated Void.

champions.title: The Dark Knight Redeemed
champions.coreFantasy: Atoning knight who chooses sacrifice or protection through stance.
champions.lore: A Dark Knight who turned against his own kingdom's cruelty and climbed Mount Ordeals to become a Paladin, trading darkness for light. In Dissidia both halves of his journey live within him: the sacrificing Dark Knight and the protecting Paladin. He chooses, moment to moment, which self the fight demands.
champions.playstyle: A dual-stance frontliner who flexes between aggression and protection. Dark Knight abilities cost health to deal heavy damage and fill a Light gauge; Paladin abilities spend that gauge to shield and heal efficiently. Cecil rewards players who read the fight and switch stance at the right beat.
champions.strengths: Highly flexible; strong self-sustain via stance cycling; can flex from bruiser to protector; good all-around durability.
champions.weaknesses: Jack-of-all-trades damage; health costs punish greedy Dark play; stance mismanagement leaves him without the tool he needs; no long-range threat.
champions.tips: Farm and poke in Dark Knight to fill the Light gauge, then Redemption into Paladin before a teamfight to spend it on shields. Cover (Paladin W) leaps to guard a diving ally — time it for the enemy's burst. Don't sit in Dark Knight at low health; the self-damage adds up fast.

passive.name: Dual Nature
passive.notes: Dark Knight damage fills a Light gauge; Paladin abilities spend it for stronger effects.

q.name: Darkness / Holy Edge
q.notes: Health-cost cleave (Dark) or restorative light slash (Paladin) depending on stance.

w.name: Shadow March / Cover
w.notes: Pressure aura (Dark) or leap to shield an ally (Paladin).

ultimate.name: Redemption
ultimate.notes: Swaps stance instantly, cleanses Cecil, and empowers the new stance for a window.

champions.title: Dragoon of the Highwind
champions.coreFantasy: Aerial initiator with commitment and precise landing zones.
champions.lore: Captain of the Baron Dragoons and Cecil's closest rival, a proud warrior whose loyalty was tested by manipulation and jealousy. His spear reaches the heavens. In Dissidia he leaps beyond sight and crashes down like a falling star, the ultimate high-risk, high-commitment engager.
champions.playstyle: A dive assassin defined by his aerial ultimate. Kain marks and slows a target with Dragon Pin, then High Jumps off-screen to select a landing zone and slam down for a knock-up. His Dragoon's Poise passive speeds him toward isolated targets, so he excels at picking off stragglers.
champions.strengths: Elite pick potential; strong single-target burst and lockdown; High Jump dodges enemy abilities while airborne; punishes poor positioning.
champions.weaknesses: All-in and telegraphed; if High Jump whiffs he's exposed on landing; weak sustained damage; needs a follow-up from allies to secure kills.
champions.tips: Land Dragon Pin FIRST so the slow guarantees your High Jump lands. While airborne you're untargetable — use it to dodge a key ability, not just to travel. Vault over walls to reset chases or escape. Pair Kain with a follow-up stun; his knock-up sets it up perfectly.

passive.name: Dragoon's Poise
passive.notes: Moving toward an isolated enemy grants bonus movement speed.

q.name: Lancet Thrust
q.notes: Linear stab that heals when it hits a champion.

w.name: Vault
w.notes: Short hop over terrain with a landing strike.

e.name: Dragon Pin
e.notes: Spear toss that marks and slows the target.

ultimate.name: High Jump
ultimate.notes: Leaps off the battlefield (untargetable), selects a landing area, then crashes down and knocks up.

champions.title: The Wandering Mimic
champions.coreFantasy: Flexible adventurer whose borrowed jobs answer the match.
champions.lore: An easygoing wanderer who inherited his father's promise to protect the world's crystals, mastering countless jobs on his journey. In Dissidia, Bartz mimics the techniques of every hero he's met, a cheerful generalist who can adapt his kit to whatever the battle throws at him.
champions.playstyle: The ultimate expression-of-mastery fighter. Bartz configures a loadout of borrowed job actions before the match, then weaves elements through Spellblade Arc and unleashes his chosen trio with Job Parade. His Freelancer passive draws small bonuses from every item category, rewarding versatile builds and clever sequencing.
champions.strengths: Extremely flexible; can be built for burst, sustain, or utility; adapts to any composition; high mastery ceiling.
champions.weaknesses: No single dominant strength; loadout choices are committed pre-match; demands deep game knowledge; average raw stats.
champions.tips: Pick your Job Parade loadout to cover your team's gaps — engage, sustain, or waveclear. Spellblade Arc's element changes the secondary effect; match it to the enemy (e.g., slow vs mobility). Guard Job converts incoming damage to speed — activate it as you commit, then reposition. Bartz is a scalpel; plan your combo before you engage.

passive.name: Freelancer
passive.notes: Gains small bonuses from each distinct item category owned.

q.name: Spellblade Arc
q.notes: Choose a temporary element that changes the secondary effect (slow, burn, or heal).

w.name: Ranger Step
w.notes: Mobile ranged strike that can be fired while repositioning.

e.name: Guard Job
e.notes: Brief stance converting part of incoming damage into movement speed.

ultimate.name: Job Parade
ultimate.notes: Cycles three empowered job actions chosen from a pre-match loadout.

champions.title: Tyrant of the Great Void
champions.coreFantasy: Immovable void tyrant who punishes poor positioning.
champions.lore: An ancient tree that absorbed centuries of sealed evil until it took armored form, seeking to consume all existence into the Void. In Dissidia, Exdeath is an implacable wall of dark power who plants himself on the battlefield and dares his enemies to approach his roots.
champions.playstyle: A tanky control mage who trades mobility for raw presence. Rooted in the Void rewards standing still with bonus defenses and stores energy he releases on the move. Exdeath anchors a zone with Black Branch and Gravity Well, dragging enemies into his patterned Grand Cross detonations.
champions.strengths: Very durable for a mage; strong area control and pull; punishes clustered or immobile enemies; excellent zone denial around objectives.
champions.weaknesses: Extremely low mobility; kited easily by ranged poke; predictable if enemies respect his zones; long ultimate wind-up.
champions.tips: Hold ground to bank Rooted in the Void defenses, then move to unleash stored energy at the right moment. Gravity Well into Black Branch drags enemies onto the delayed roots. Void Gate can redirect your own projectiles around a wall — or let one ally slip through. Grand Cross is avoidable, so pair it with Gravity Well to trap them inside.

passive.name: Rooted in the Void
passive.notes: Standing still increases defenses and stores void energy released on the next move/cast.

q.name: Black Branch
q.notes: Line of dark roots that erupts after a short delay.

e.name: Void Gate
e.notes: Paired short portals for projectiles and one champion passage.

ultimate.name: Grand Cross
ultimate.notes: Large patterned zone with sequential, avoidable detonations and random debuffs.
